DS 4420 - Spring 2026
Bayesian Logistic Regression: Predicting Spotify Top 10
Dhruv Laungani & Lucas Tolman


```{r}
library(brms)
library(ggplot2)

# loads
df <- read.csv("arma_features.csv")
df$top10 <- as.factor(df$top10)

# log-scale mean_streams
df$log_mean_streams <- log(df$mean_streams)

# standardize
predictors <- c("ar1_coef", "ma1_coef", "log_mean_streams", "trend_slope",
                "volatility", "early_late_ratio",
                "danceability", "energy", "valence",
                "acousticness", "loudness", "speechiness")

df_scaled <- df
df_scaled[, predictors] <- scale(df[, predictors])

# train/test split — 80/20
set.seed(42)
idx        <- sample(1:nrow(df_scaled), floor(0.8 * nrow(df_scaled)))
train      <- df_scaled[ idx, ]
test       <- df_scaled[-idx, ]
 
cat("Train:", nrow(train), "| Test:", nrow(test), "\n")
cat("Top10 in train:\n"); print(table(train$top10))

# priors
default_prior(top10 ~ ar1_coef + ma1_coef + log_mean_streams + trend_slope +
                       volatility + early_late_ratio +
                       danceability + energy + valence +
                       acousticness + loudness + speechiness,
              data = train,
              family = bernoulli("logit"))

# logistic regression on standardized predictors
manual_prior <- c(
  prior(student_t(4, 0, 5), class = "Intercept"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "ar1_coef"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "ma1_coef"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "log_mean_streams"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "trend_slope"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "volatility"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "early_late_ratio"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "danceability"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "energy"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "valence"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "acousticness"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "loudness"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "speechiness")
)


# fit model
fit <- brm(
  top10 ~ ar1_coef + ma1_coef + log_mean_streams + trend_slope +
          volatility + early_late_ratio +
          danceability + energy + valence +
          acousticness + loudness + speechiness,
  family = bernoulli("logit"),
  data = train,
  prior = manual_prior,
  chains = 4,
  iter = 2000,
  warmup = 500,
  thin = 2,
  cores = 4,
  seed = 42
)


# summarize
summary(fit)


# posterior coeff plot
mcmc_plot(fit, type = "intervals", prob = 0.80, prob_outer = 0.95) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Posterior Coefficient Estimates (80% and 95% CI)",
       subtitle = "Features with intervals not crossing zero are credibly predictive",
       x = "Coefficient estimate (log-odds scale)",
       y = "") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)


# conditional effects
plot(conditional_effects(fit, "log_mean_streams"),
     theme = theme_minimal()) 

plot(conditional_effects(fit, "ar1_coef"),
     theme = theme_minimal())

plot(conditional_effects(fit, "trend_slope"),
     theme = theme_minimal())

plot(conditional_effects(fit, "energy"),
     theme = theme_minimal())


# test set predictions
post_preds <- posterior_predict(fit, newdata = test)
pred_probs <- colMeans(post_preds == "1")
pred_class <- ifelse(pred_probs >= 0.5, 1, 0)
true_class <- as.numeric(as.character(test$top10))

# accuracy and confusion matrix
accuracy <- mean(pred_class == true_class)
cat("Test Accuracy:", round(accuracy, 3), "\n")
print(table(Predicted = pred_class, Actual = true_class))

# posterior predictive distribution for a single example song
high_idx <- which(test$log_mean_streams == max(test$log_mean_streams))[1]
low_idx  <- which(test$log_mean_streams == min(test$log_mean_streams))[1]

hist(post_preds[, high_idx],
     main = paste("Post. Pred. Dist —", test$title[high_idx]),
     xlab = "Predicted Top 10", col = "steelblue")

hist(post_preds[, low_idx],
     main = paste("Post. Pred. Dist —", test$title[low_idx]),
     xlab = "Predicted Top 10", col = "salmon")


# posterior sigmoid distributions for two example songs
post_draws <- as.data.frame(fit)

sigmoid <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-x))

post_prob <- function(song_row) {
  x <- as.numeric(song_row[predictors])
  lp <- post_draws$b_Intercept +
        post_draws$b_ar1_coef * x[1] +
        post_draws$b_ma1_coef * x[2] +
        post_draws$b_log_mean_streams * x[3] +
        post_draws$b_trend_slope * x[4] +
        post_draws$b_volatility * x[5] +
        post_draws$b_early_late_ratio * x[6] +
        post_draws$b_danceability * x[7] +
        post_draws$b_energy * x[8] +
        post_draws$b_valence * x[9] +
        post_draws$b_acousticness * x[10] +
        post_draws$b_loudness * x[11] +
        post_draws$b_speechiness * x[12]
  sigmoid(lp)
}

probs_high <- post_prob(test[high_idx, ])
probs_low  <- post_prob(test[low_idx,  ])

hist(probs_high,
     main = paste("P(Top 10) —", test$title[high_idx]),
     xlab = "Posterior probability", col = "steelblue", xlim = c(0, 1))
abline(v = mean(probs_high), col = "red", lwd = 2)

hist(probs_low,
     main = paste("P(Top 10) —", test$title[low_idx]),
     xlab = "Posterior probability", col = "salmon", xlim = c(0, 1))
abline(v = mean(probs_low), col = "red", lwd = 2)

cat("Mean P(Top 10) for high song:", round(mean(probs_high), 3), "\n")
cat("Mean P(Top 10) for low song: ", round(mean(probs_low),  3), "\n")

```
